newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - June 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - June 6.

text.p: The following are the highlights of stories from the Irish press on Friday.

- The threat of another interest rate rise grew last night as latest figures from the central bank showed no sign of a slowdown in the borrowing boom or lessening of the difficulties facing the Irish pound.
- A majority of voters in Friday's election reject a coalition between Fianna Fail and Labour in the event of a hung parliament, an Irish Independent poll said.
- A French-style blockade closed Dublin port last night as angry irish truckers demonstrated in a row over charges paid by shipping firms.

- The Irish and British governments are preparing a joint paper calling for decommissioning to be addressed during substantive talks in line with a report by ex-Senator George Mitchell rather than in advance of the talks.
- Political leaders urged the Republic's 2.7 million voters to turn out in large numbers for Friday's election.

- Britishs Nuclear Fuels' latest monitoring figures indicate that concentration of radioactive Technetium 99 found in lobsters off the West Cumbrian coast near Sellafield have risen to unprecedented levels.
